notable_absence.finding: Like learn/security/certificates.md (round-batch sibling), this procedural page has no mention of certificate revocation, CRLs, or OCSP anywhere across two full client-certificate-creation walkthroughs (root-signed and intermediate-signed) plus the Java-client keystore walkthrough. The only way a page in this batch describes to stop trusting an already-issued client certificate before its expiry is removing the signing CA from the cluster's trust store entirely (documented on configure-server-certificates.md, this same batch) - which revokes every certificate that CA ever signed, not the one compromised certificate. This corroborates, from the administration-procedure side, the same first-order PKI-lifecycle gap the reference layer already showed.

cross_component_finding: The page's Java-client section is a genuinely separate procedure surface from the OpenSSL-based Couchbase Server/CDCR client-certificate procedures above it: it uses `keytool` and a keystore file, not `openssl` and PEM files, to hold the identical root+client certificate pair generated by the same upstream openssl commands. No other product in the corpus's cert:/tls: namespaces has a client-side certificate CONTAINER concept (a keystore) modeled at all - every other client-certificate relation in the registry (e.g. cert:client-certificate verifiesIdentityOf) treats the certificate as a bare artifact, not something itself held inside a further, distinct storage construct. This is the round's clearest new admin-facing mechanism in this page: cert:java-keystore.
cross_product_finding: The XDCR use case (source cluster securely replicating to a destination cluster using a client certificate) is stated here only as a one-sentence aside with a forward link to manage-xdcr/enable-full-secure-replication.md; this page itself never explains how XDCR consumes the certificate (e.g. whether the destination cluster's Couchbase Server instance treats the source cluster as just another authenticating 'client' for RBAC purposes). That relationship - XDCR-as-a-client-of-the-remote-cluster's-RBAC - is asserted by reliesOnMechanism above but is otherwise undocumented on this page; a docs-issue candidate for whichever round covers manage-xdcr in depth.
